name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-25EM 'Tempest'
description:
The KPA-25EM Tempest is Kang-Petrov's second-generation electromagnetic rifle, addressing the Thunderclap's limitations with a dual-stage acceleration system and improved capacitor technology. The Tempest fires 4mm tungsten-composite penetrators — an upgrade from the Thunderclap's steel-core rounds — and achieves velocities approaching the Arcturus MAR-8X at two-thirds the cost.

Kang-Petrov's engineering team reverse-engineered the acceleration physics from captured MAR-8X units and developed their own implementation using commercially available components. The Tempest's capacitor system is distributed through the weapon's body rather than concentrated in a single pack, reducing the catastrophic failure risk that plagues Thunderclap modifications. Power supply provides 50 shots per charge with a 60-second recharge cycle.

Arcturus has filed seventeen patent infringement claims against the Tempest, all of which Kang-Petrov has contested in corporate arbitration. The legal battle has become a proxy war over whether electromagnetic weapons technology can be monopolized. Meanwhile, the Tempest ships to any buyer with Φ8,000 and standard licensing.
specifications:
caliber: 4mm tungsten-composite penetrator
effective_range: 650m
rate_of_fire: 180 rpm (capacitor-limited)
magazine_capacity: 50 penetrators per charge
weight: 4.1 kg
tactical_use: The Tempest provides near-military electromagnetic capability to operators outside the corporate military pipeline. Its tungsten-composite penetrators defeat Level III armor at engagement range, and the distributed capacitor system eliminates the single-point failure that makes Thunderclap modifications dangerous. The weapon functions as a squad-level anti-armor asset for forces that cannot afford or access Arcturus platforms.
cultural_context: The Tempest is a direct challenge to Arcturus' dominance in electromagnetic weapons, and the ongoing legal battle has made it a symbol of resistance against corporate technology monopolies. Buying a Tempest is partly a practical decision and partly a political statement. Kang-Petrov prints 'INNOVATION CANNOT BE MONOPOLIZED' on every Tempest shipping crate.
story_hooks: Arcturus has lost patience with legal channels and is planning a covert operation to sabotage Kang-Petrov's Tempest manufacturing facility.

A Tempest purchased through legitimate channels came with hidden firmware that scans for and logs the presence of nearby Arcturus equipment — Kang-Petrov is building an intelligence map of Arcturus deployments through their customers' weapons.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular assault rifle with a distinctly modular appearance. The KPA-25EM Tempest presents as a refined second-generation platform—less brutish than its Thunderclap predecessor, with clean lines and purposeful ergonomics. The weapon suggests precision engineering rather than improvised power, with distributed components along the receiver creating subtle visual rhythm. The profile is aggressive but controlled, built for professional operators rather than chrome-heavy enthusiasts.
physical_description.dimensions: 1,045mm overall length, 85mm width at receiver, 65mm height at charging handle. 385mm barrel with progressive electromagnetic coil geometry visible through translucent polymer sections.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced. 4.1 kg distributed evenly across the frame prevents muzzle-heaviness. Feels substantial in the hands—a weapon engineered for extended engagements without fatigue compensation.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed aluminum receiver with reinforced polymer furniture. Distributed capacitor housing uses carbon-composite panels along the handguard and upper receiver. Barrel assembly is hardened steel with embedded electromagnetic induction coils.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal-gray anodized aluminum with satin-black polymer accents. Tactical rail surfaces feature light tool marks suggesting functional design priority. Some units show micro-texturing for grip security.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with jet-black polymer components. Accent pieces in dark bronze where capacitor modules interface. Status LEDs glow amber during charge cycle.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with integrated capacitive charge indicators. Handguard features aggressive crosshatch pattern for secure grip, even with liquid polymer combat gloves. Magazine well has subtle ribbing for positive insertion feedback.
distinctive_features: Translucent polymer access panels along upper receiver exposing internal electromagnetic coil progression
Distributed capacitor module covers with segmented design—four visible segments running length of weapon
Integrated charge status indicator strip running along right side of receiver (amber when charging, green when ready)
Electromagnetic rail system mounted at 0° and 45° angles for optics and auxiliary systems
Muzzle brake designed as electromagnetic flux director—unconventional geometry with slotted venting
Quick-disconnect capacitor coupling system visible at rear receiver
Heat-dissipation vents along capacitor segments with angular, almost art-deco aesthetic
Serial number plate (KPA-25EM series) laser-etched on left receiver
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: KANG-PETROV ARMS in crisp sans-serif font stamped on left side of upper receiver. KPA logo (stylized linked geometric shapes) embossed on charging handle. 'TEMPEST' designation etched below safety selector in smaller text.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field weapons typically show light surface wear on polymer handguards and minor scuffing on aluminum receiver. Capacitor module covers often display dust accumulation around cooling vents. Well-maintained units show no corrosion; heavily used examples may have abraded finish around magazine well and charging handle from repeated manipulation.
